response.query: Which lawful basis will we apply per data type (consent vs public interest), how will we document Art.9(2)(j) use if special categories appear, and what are practical withdrawal mechanics?
response.answer: For special categories, lawful basis is consent or public interest (Art. 9(2)(j)). Document use with evidence of public interest. Withdrawal must be straightforward and effective.

results.title: Data (Use and Access) Bill [HL] - Hansard
results.content: Amendments 59 and 62, by inserting the word “solely” into proposed new paragraphs 2 and 3 in Clause 67, would disaggregate reuse of data for scientific research purposes from other purposes, ensuring that the only goal of reuse is scientific research. The Government need to provide reassurance that the intention and impact of the research provisions are not to enable the reuse of personal data, as the noble Viscount said, scraped from the internet or collected by tech companies under legitimate interest for training AI. Amendment 64, taken together with those tabled by the noble Viscount that I have signed, would radically reduce the scope for misuse of data reuse provisions by ensuring that controllers cannot mix their commercial purposes with scientific research and that such research must be in the public interest and conducted in line with established academic practice for genuine scientific research, such as ethics approval.
